category: newly launched institutional repository (InvenioRDM 14, KTH Royal Institute of Technology)

free_tier.stated: By default, up to 100 files with a total size of 30 GB (30,000,000,000 bytes) per record; each file up to 30 GB. Quota increase is granted on request to researchdata@kth.se.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: Each file can be up to 30 GB, within the record's total quota.

retention.stated: You can **only delete an unpublished record**. Published records cannot be deleted except under special circumstances. If necessary, please submit a request via our support line.
retention.notes: A **one-month grace period** allows file modifications if errors are found. After this period, changes are only permitted in justified cases (e.g., copyright infringement, exposure of personal data).

egress.terms: Free and anonymous access. Download links return HTTP 302 redirecting to presigned S3 URLs with 60-second expiration, requiring per-request URL resolution.

interface_detail: The REST API calls for KTH Datarepository require authentication. The currently supported authentication method is through the use of Bearer tokens, which can be generated in the "Applications" section of your user account's settings in the KTH Datarepository.
chaining: In the **Files** section of the deposit form, click the **Import files** button to import files from a previous version. Using this feature saves storage space as we don't duplicate the previous files.
limits_note: 100 files per record by default. 'For data governance reasons ... all data must belong to at least one community.' Files immutable after publication; one-month grace period.
reliability_note: Login is ORCID / GitHub / KTH SSO. Genuinely open. But deposit requires membership of a KTH community, and the quota-increase email asks which 'organisation, project, or grant' the data belongs to.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.

extras.egress_verbatim: Free and anonymous. Downloads 302 to presigned.s3.cloud.kth.se with X-Amz-Expires=60 — sixty seconds, so rule 8 applies hard: re-resolve per request or watch every parallel GET return an empty 302.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Mountable via any InvenioRDM wrapper; the 60-second presign makes it a poor CDN origin unless fronted by Cloudflare with a re-resolving shim.
extras.agent_focus: Two client questions. (1) Open academic infrastructure that does NOT validate institutional identity — for each repository I probed the machine-readable quota endpoint (GET /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota, /api/records?size=1, /api/info/version) rather than trusting marketing pages, and separately tested the write gate, because open-signup-with-unlimited-quota and open-signup-with-deposit-rights are different things and this wave exists to separate them. (2) Relay/P2P, split into signalling (coordinates only) vs relaying (data transits, operator pays). Secondary sweep: the 2025-26 AI data commons (FineWeb, Common Pile, DCLM, Dolma, Pleias) to establish whether any of them offers writable storage — none does; they are all read-only distribution on HF or Common Crawl S3, i.e. egress sources, not deposit targets. Dataverse turns out to be the only architecture in this space that ships a quota API that answers 'is there a limit' in one GET, so I ran it across every instance I could reach.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
